rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse first names guidance as a genus, then singles out its clear kinds; this honorific coordination intensifies the description through three levels, and the clear mode is the superior division.
rows.anchor: والأول أفضل القسمين فذكر الجنس أولا ثم أردفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing the month here means being present at one's place of residence, whether a town or village.
rows.anchor: حضر موضع الإقامة من المصر أو القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-shahr is accusative as a temporal adverb, not an object, because both residents and travelers witness the month.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الظرف أي : في الشهر دون المفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means let him fast in it: a preposition is omitted and the verb is extended directly to the governed noun.
rows.anchor: فليصم فيه بحذف الجار وإيصال الفعل إلى المجرور اتساعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resident who must fast is a rational, mature, healthy person; children and the insane may be present in town but are not obligated.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالشاهد العاقل البالغ الصحيح لأن كل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This binding command abrogates the resident's former choice between fasting, breaking the fast, and paying fidya.
rows.anchor: ينسخ التخيير بين الصوم والإفطار والفداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The illness concession applies even to a resident, and the travel concession even to a healthy person; ʿalā here means fī.
rows.anchor: وإن كان مقيما حاضرا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sick person or traveler who breaks the fast must make up the missed days later.
rows.anchor: فعليه صيام أيام أخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier verse allowed residents able to fast, travelers, and the sick to choose; this verse removes the resident's choice, so the concession is restated to show it remains for the sick and traveler.
rows.anchor: وأعاد تخيير المريض والمسافر وترخيصهما في الإفطار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God intends ease by permitting breaking the fast during travel or illness; yusr means what is made easy.
rows.anchor: حيث أباح الفطر بالسفر والمرض واليسر ما تسهل

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reads ease as Paradise and hardship as Hell: fasting is intended to bring the servant into Paradise and spare him entry into Hell.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن علي الترمذي قدس سره : اليسر اسم الجنة

rows.speaker: الفضلي
rows.claim: Al-Faḍlī says fasting brings ease in both abodes: worldly spiritual ascent and wakefulness toward knowledge, then Paradise, blessing, nearness, union, and vision; hardship is worldly animal and ego-bound life, then Hell and its torments.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا العلامة الفضلي قدس سره في الآية أن مراده تعالى بأن يأمركم بالصوم

rows.speaker: نجم الدين
rows.claim: Najm al-Dīn says to attend to the ease that accompanies hardship while obeying a command; like a patient taking bitter medicine for health, the wise focus on its benefit and drink with resolve.
rows.anchor: وقال نجم الدين في "تأويلاته" : يعني يريد الله بكم

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī's couplet illustrates that a wise physician's bitter medicine is beneficial, like sugar given to a sick person.
rows.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره : وبالست دادن برنجور قند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the prescribed total means making up the days missed because of illness or travel after Ramadan's fast was imposed.
rows.anchor: فعليكم عدة ما أفطرتم لتكملوا عدد أيام الشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction to make up fasts on later days leaves their arrangement unrestricted, so they may be consecutive or separated; magnifying God means praising Him.
rows.anchor: إنما علمناكم كيفية القضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is a verbal noun: the phrase means praising God for guiding you to a way of discharging the duty.
rows.anchor: ما مصدرية أي : على هدايته إياكم إلى طريق الخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fast-breaking concession is granted so that people thank God for this blessing with tongue, heart, and body.
rows.anchor: إنما رخصنا لكم بالإفطار لكي تشكروا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says whoever keeps three things is truly God's friend, and whoever neglects them is truly God's enemy: prayer, fasting, and the bath after major ritual impurity; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: الصلاة والصوم والغسل من الجنابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Paradise longs for four groups: Ramadan fasters, Qurʾan reciters, those who guard their tongues, and those who feed neighbors; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: إن الجنان يشتقن إلى أربعة نفر صائمي رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God forgives the Muslim at iftar for the sins of the limbs and thoughts his body and heart have engaged in; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: وإن الله يغفر للعبد المسلم عند إفطاره ما مشت إليه رجلاه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet reports seeing at the Lote Tree a vast, radiant angel assigned to glorify God on behalf of him and his community for Ramadan; two locked chests before the angel hold the community's deliverance from Hell, and no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qāshānī maps the time of pilgrimage across three ages from puberty to forty, each like a month: growth, the inner secret of standing, and part of middle age, likened to the cow between old and young.
rows.anchor: وقال القاشاني : وقت الحج أزمنة وهو من وقت بلوغ الحلم إلى الأربعين

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Ḥāfiẓ's cited couplet calls love, youth, and free-spiritedness the complete desired collection, whose combination enables expression.
rows.anchor: قال الحافظ : عشق وشباب ورندى مجموعه مرادست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Junāḥ means sin, from junūḥ, inclination away from the straight course.
rows.anchor: إثم من الجنوح وهو الميل عن القصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking bounty from God means pursuing trade and livelihood during pilgrimage; the verse answered those who claimed merchants and camel drivers could not perform Hajj.
rows.anchor: عطاء ورزقا منه يريد الربح بالتجارة في أيام الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trade during Hajj is permissible, but leaving it is preferable because worship should be done sincerely, with no motive beyond obedience.
rows.anchor: التجارة وإن كانت مباحة في الحج إلا أن الأولى تركها فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In afadtum, the hamza is causative and the object is omitted; the phrase depicts a large crowd leaving ʿArafāt after sunset and returning from the standing.
rows.anchor: الهمزة في أفضتم للتعدية والمفعول محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The essential sense of ifāḍa here is a large group joining in departure and travel.
rows.anchor: حقيقة الإفاضة هنا هو اجتماع الكثير في الذهاب والمسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿArafāt is a proper name for the place of standing, not a true plural; its added letters intensify the sense of knowing.
rows.anchor: وعرفات علم للموقف وليس بجمع حقيقة بل هو من قبيل ما زيدت حروفه لزيادة معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Gabriel identified the pilgrimage site to Abraham; when Abraham saw it, he recognized it and it was named ʿArafāt.
rows.anchor: روي أنه نعته جبريل لإبراهيم عليهما السلام فلما أبصره عرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation derives the name from Gabriel's circuit of the ritual sites as he asked Abraham whether he knew them, to which Abraham answered that he did.
rows.anchor: كان يدور به في المشاعر أي : مواضع المناسك ويقول : عرفت فيقول : عرفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says Adam descended in India and Eve in Jeddah; after searching for each other, they met and recognized one another at ʿArafāt.
rows.anchor: آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام لما أهبط إلى الأرض وقع بالهند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Standing at ʿArafāt is obligatory because the command to depart from it presupposes being present and standing there, and what is necessary to fulfill an obligation is itself obligatory.
rows.anchor: دليل على وجوب الوقوف بعرفات لأن الإضافة مأمور بها وهي موقوفة على الحضور فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance at the Sacred Monument includes the talbiya, declaration of divine unity, glorification, praise, laudation, and supplications.
rows.anchor: بالتلبية والتهليل والتسبيح والتحميد والثناء والدعوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sacred Monument is Qazaḥ, the mountain where the imam stands at al-Mīqada.
rows.anchor: قزح وهو الجبل الذي يقف عليه الإمام وعلى الميقدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After completing the acts of worship prescribed for Hajj, believers should devote themselves to remembering God.
rows.anchor: أتممتم عباداتكم التي أمرتم بها في الحج وفرغتم منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Minā, Arabs used to recall their ancestors' boasts and glorious days to gain fame and status; God forbade that habit and ordered His own praise and remembrance in its place.
rows.anchor: وكانت العرب إذا قضوا مناسكهم وقفوا بمنى بين المسجد والجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is the source of all good; ancestors are His servants and obtained their achievements through His grace, so His praise should replace boasting about them.
rows.anchor: إذ الخير كله من عنده وآباؤهم عبيده ونالوا ما نالوا بأفضاله

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī's couplet says that good comes from God through divine enabling, not from one servant independently reaching another.
rows.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره : كراز حق نه توفيق خيري رسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean remembering God as much as one remembered ancestors, or with even more intense remembrance; the genitive coordination figuratively treats remembrance as a rememberer.
rows.anchor: مجرور معطوف على الذكر بجعله ذاكرا على المجاز أي : اذكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An adjective in an annexed construction normally shares the preceding noun's category, while an accusative complement can differ; here the annexation is justified by personifying remembrance as remembering another remembrance.
rows.anchor: أفعل إنما يضاف إلى ما بعده إذا كان من جنس ما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing remembrance to remembrance is possible figuratively when one hears a mention and thereby remembers, so the first remembrance seems to have remembered.
rows.anchor: ويجوز نسبة الذكر إلى الذكر بأن يسمع إنسان الذكر فيذكر

words: فَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who ask only for worldly gifts such as status, wealth, and victory are polytheists, whose Hajj supplication seeks only immediate worldly advantage.
rows.anchor: في ذكره مقتصرا على طلب الدنيا

words: وَمَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because such a person's concern is confined to this world, he has no share in the Hereafter: at the holiest standing he asked for the lowest goods and neglected lasting bliss.
rows.anchor: همه مقصور على الدنيا حيث سأل في أعز المواقف أحقر المطالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other pilgrims ask for the good of both abodes, including health, sufficiency, and enabling grace to do good.
rows.anchor: هي الصحة والكفاف والتوفيق للخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Mathnawī couplet urges disciplining the soul away from Satan, keeping angelic company, and feeding it lawful sustenance that brings light and perfection.
rows.anchor: طفل جان ازشير شيطان بازكن بعد ازانش باملك انباز كن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Companions were exceptionally good: they asked the Messenger only thirteen questions, all answered in the Qurʾan, and asked only about matters beneficial to them and Muslims.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ما رأيت قوما كانوا خيرا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما سألوه إلا عن ثلاث عشرة مسألة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is about the ruling on consuming wine, since permissibility, prohibition, sin, and obedience attach to accountable acts, not to objects in themselves; the ruling also covers sale and purchase.
rows.anchor: عن حكم تعاطيها بقرينة الجواب لأن الحل والحرمة والإثم والطاعة إنما هي من عوارض أفعال المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khamr is named from the root for covering: grape juice that boils, thickens, and foams covers the intellect and discernment, as though it were itself a veil.
rows.anchor: والخمر مصدر خمره أي : ستره سمي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maisir is a verbal noun from yasara; it may be named for taking wealth easily without labor or for impoverishing the loser.
rows.anchor: مصدر ميمي من يسر كالموعد والمرجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maisir includes every kind of gambling, chess, and even children's games with walnuts and dice.
rows.anchor: ويدخل فيه جميع أنواع القمار والشطرنج وغيرهما حتى لعب الصبيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase refers to engaging in and using wine and gambling.
rows.anchor: في تعاطي الخمر والميسر واستعمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their grave sin is that wine destroys reason, the pivot of religion and worldly life, and both wine and gambling ruin wealth.
rows.anchor: مسلبة للعقول التي هي قطب الدين والدنيا مع كون كل منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine had perceived benefits including exhilaration, resale profit, strengthening the weak, aiding digestion and sex, easing grief, emboldening the fearful, loosening the miser's hand, improving complexion, and stirring speech and resolve.
rows.anchor: من كسب الطرب والمغالاة بثمن الخمر إذا جلبوها من الأطراف وفيها تقوية الضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gambling could bring unearned money and meat for the poor, since winners distributed the camel's meat to people in need.
rows.anchor: ومنافع الميسر إصابة المال من غير كد ولا تعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine incites enmity and hatred and diverts from remembrance of God and prayer; it makes the sensible foolish, as illustrated by an obscene drunkard's behavior.
rows.anchor: وفي الخمر إيقاع العداوة والبغضاء والصد عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الدنيا
rows.claim: Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recounts seeing a drunkard urinate into his hand, wipe his face as if performing ablution, and praise Islam and water; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: كما ذكر ابن أبي الدنيا أنه مر على سكران وهو يبول في يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a gambler loses his money without compensation, he resents the winner, becomes his enemy, and seeks to harm him.
rows.anchor: وفي الميسر أنه إذا ذهب ماله من غير عوض ساءه ذلك فعادى صاحبه

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators describe a four-stage prohibition: the first, Meccan verse mentioned wine made from dates and grapes alongside good provision, and Muslims initially drank it as lawful.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون تواردت في الخمر أربع آيات نزلت

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: After ʿUmar, Muʿādh, and other Companions asked about wine because it removes reason, the verse on wine and gambling was revealed; some tried to take its benefits while avoiding its sin, while others abstained.
rows.anchor: افتنا يا رسول الله في الخمر فإنها مذهبة للعقل فنزلت

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: At a gathering hosted by ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, a drunken reciter omitted the negation in Sūrat al-Kāfirūn; the prayer-time prohibition followed.
rows.anchor: قام أحدهم فقرأ قل يا أيها الكافرون أعبد ما تعبدون

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: After the prayer-time restriction, some still drank outside prayer hours, expecting to sober up between the evening or dawn prayer and the next prayer.
rows.anchor: وشربها قوم في غير حين الصلاة حتى كان الرجل يشربها بعد صلاة العشاء

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: At ʿItbān ibn Mālik's feast, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ recited a poem insulting the Anṣār and praising his clan; a guest struck and wounded Saʿd with a camel's jawbone, after which Saʿd complained to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: ثم اتخذ عتبان بن مالك ضيافة ودعا رجالا من المسلمين فيهم سعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: After Saʿd's injury, ʿUmar prayed for a decisive clarification; the final prohibition verses were then revealed and he answered that they had desisted.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر : اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine was prohibited in the third year after the Hijra, a few days after the Battle of the Trench.
rows.anchor: وحرمت الخمر في السنة الثالثة من الهجرة بعد غزوة الأحزاب بأيام

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffāl explains the staged ban as gentle instruction: people were accustomed to wine and benefited from it, so an immediate prohibition would have burdened them; after the final ruling, it was poured out.
rows.anchor: قال القفال والحكمة في وقوع التحريم على هذا الترتيب

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that when the final ban came, some Companions broke their wine jars and others washed them with water and clay; rain later revealed wine's color and smell in Medina's streets for a time.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما : خرجنا بالحباب إلى الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wine had been exceptionally beloved to the Arabs, and God prohibited nothing more forcefully than it.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن يومئذ للعرب عيش أعجب منها وما حرم الله عليهم شيئا أشد من الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As outward wine comes from grapes, dates, raisins, and grains, inward wine comes from heedlessness, desire, caprice, and love of the world; these intoxicate the human soul and intellect and are sinful.
rows.anchor: والإشارة في الآية أن خمر الظاهر كما يتخذ من أجناس مختلفة من العنب والتمر والزبيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since intoxicants are sinful, every intoxicant is forbidden, and anything whose large amount intoxicates is forbidden even in a small amount.
rows.anchor: ولهذا كل مسكر حرام وما يسكر كثيره فقليله حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A different spiritual wine intoxicates hearts, spirits, and secrets: it is the drink of spiritual arrivals in cups of witnessing, poured by the cupbearer of divine attributes' self-disclosure.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما يسكر القلوب والأرواح والأسرار فهو شراب الواردات في أقداح المشاهدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That spiritual drink quiets appetites; hearts are absorbed in ecstasies, spirits in witnessing, and secrets in the glimpse of beauty, so it is beneficial and lawful.
rows.anchor: فإذا دارت على النفوس وانخمدت شهواتها وسكرت القلوب بالمواجيد عن المواحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some are intoxicated by the drink's existence, others by witnessing its cupbearer; a couplet contrasts their states.
rows.anchor: فالعجب كل العجب أن قوما أسكرهم وجود الشراب وقوما أسكرهم شهود الساقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the spiritual journey, turning away from the cups of union at the end is a greater loss than a thousand years of seeking at the beginning is a gain.
rows.anchor: وأتم الإعراض عن كؤوس الوصال في النهاية أكبر من نفع الطلب ألف سنة في البداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as a wine-drunk person is barred from prayer, one drunk with heedlessness and caprice is veiled from communion.
rows.anchor: سكران الغفلة والهوى محجوب عن المواصلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward sin of gambling is the prevalence of trickery, deception, lying, and foul speech in the way people pursue the spiritual path; it is grave to the elect and alien to the righteous.
rows.anchor: وأما إثم الميسر فهو أن آثار القمار هي شعار أكثر الديار في سلوك طريق الحيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward benefit of gambling is disregard for both worlds and effacement of worldly forms in the singularity of the Kaaba's imprint.
rows.anchor: وأما نفعه فعدم الالتفات إلى الكونين وبزل نقوش العالمين في فردانية نقش الكعبتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reading says sins outweigh benefits because the sins affect the many while benefits belong to the elect, and the many outnumber the elect.
rows.anchor: لأن إثمهما للعوام ونفعهما للخواص والعوام أكثر من الخواص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charity question continues the topic of what to spend raised by the earlier verse; when 2:215 was revealed, ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ asked what he should spend, prompting the instruction al-ʿafw.
rows.anchor: قال عمر بن الجموح ما أنفق فنزل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿafw is the opposite of effort and hardship: spend what is easy, available, and surplus to one's own needs and the needs of dependents.
rows.anchor: أنفقوا العفو وهو نقيض الجهد وهو المشقة ونقيضه اليسر والسهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf is accusative as an adjective for an omitted absolute object, meaning clarification like this; singular address can target a plural audience conceived as a group.
rows.anchor: والكاف في محل النصب صفة لمصدر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the signs concerning legal rulings clear in their import and indication, not after they were obscure or confused.
rows.anchor: الدالة على الأحكام الشرعية لا بيانا أدنى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thinking about both abodes means choosing what is better and easier in this life, what benefits in the next, and avoiding what harms one there.
rows.anchor: لكي تتفكروا في أمور الدارين فتأخذوا بما هو أصلح لكم

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawī says to reflect on the world's passing nature and renounce it, and on the Hereafter's permanence and turn toward it.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : يبين الله لكم الآيات في أمر الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A man offered the Prophet his only possession, a gold egg from a campaign, as charity. The Prophet first turned away, then angrily took and threw it, rebuking him for giving away all his wealth and leaving himself dependent; charity should come from surplus. No grading is given.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام أن رجلا أتاه ببيضة من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿafw also hints that a donor's gift should leave no trace in the heart, meaning it should be given freely and cheerfully; the root sense is erasure.
rows.anchor: وفي لفظ العفو إشارة إلى أن ما يعطيه المرء ينبغي أن يعفو أثره عن قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elect give from wealth beyond sufficiency, while the elite of the elite practice selfless preference and give what they need, even to a wealthy recipient.
rows.anchor: ثم الإخراج عن فاضل الأموال على قدر الكفاية طريقة الخواص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest form of self-preference is supported by the verse describing believers who give others priority even while themselves in need.
rows.anchor: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar donated half his wealth to outdo Abū Bakr, but when asked what remained for his family he said half; Abū Bakr gave everything, saying Allah and His Messenger remained for them, and ʿUmar conceded he would not compete again.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : أمرنا رسول الله

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet described the distance between ʿUmar and Abū Bakr as like the difference between their two answers about what they left for their families; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: روي أن النبي عليه السلام قال عند ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account shows Abū Bakr's superiority over ʿUmar in this respect, but excellence in one matter does not establish inferiority in every other matter; ranking depends on knowledge of God.
rows.anchor: ومنه يعرف فضل أبي بكر على عمر لكن الفاضلة من وجه لا تنافي المفضولية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means: has knowledge reached you with certainty comparable to direct sight? More literally, it commands the listener to know from God's report, which gives certainty.
rows.anchor: ألم ينته علمك الذي يضاهي العيان في الإيقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase refers to the story of the king who argued with Abraham about his Lord.
rows.anchor: إلى قصة الملك الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥājja means he debated, disputed, and answered an opponent with argument.
rows.anchor: جادل وخاصم وقابل بالحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to God's lordship, attached to Abraham, honors Abraham and signals that God supported him in the debate.
rows.anchor: عنوان الربوبية مع أن الإضافة إلى ضميره عليه الصلاة والسلام تشريف له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king was Nimrod son of Canaan son of Shem son of Noah, the first to wear a crown, act tyrannically, and claim divinity.
rows.anchor: هو نمرود بن كنعان بن سام بن نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is causal: God gave him sovereignty, and that is why he argued.
rows.anchor: فهو مفعول له لقوله حاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that he reversed the proper response: instead of thanking God for sovereignty, he argued with Abraham.
rows.anchor: من باب العكس في الكلام بمعنى أنه وضع المحاجة موضع الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God's granting him great wealth, ample means, and complete rule made him proud and insolent, which led him to dispute.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن إيتاء الملك حمله على ذلك لأنه أورثه الكبر والبطر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says only four people ruled the whole world: the Muslims Solomon and Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the unbelievers Nimrod and Bukht Naṣr, identified in the source with Shaddād son of ʿĀd, builder of Iram.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد لم يملك الدنيا بأسرها إلا أربعة مسلمان وكافران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's granting sovereignty to an unbeliever challenges the Muʿtazilite claim that God must do what is best for each person; empowering an unbeliever over believers may not seem best for believers, but the author says it is a trial for ruler and subjects.
rows.anchor: ثم هو حجة على من منع إيتاء الله الملك للكافر وهم المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase idh qāla is a temporal adverb attached to ḥājja.
rows.anchor: إذ قال إبراهام} ظرف لحاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abraham broke the idols, Nimrod imprisoned him and brought him out to burn him, then asked who was the Lord to whom Abraham called people.
rows.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام لما كسر الأصنام سجنه ثم أخرجه ليحرقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham means that his Lord creates life and death in bodies; this is a sound proof because God is known through attributes and acts no other powerful being shares.
rows.anchor: يخلق الحياة والممات في الأجساد وجواب إبراهيم في غاية الصحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod summoned two prisoners, killed one and released the other, then misleadingly described sparing a life as giving life.
rows.anchor: دعا برجلين قد حبسهما فقتل أحدهما وأطلق الآخر

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham answers with a decisive sign: God moves the sun from east to west by compulsion according to His will, whereas Nimrod would have to make it travel naturally the opposite way if he possessed comparable power.
rows.anchor: تحريكا قسريا حسبما تقتضيه مشيئته والباء للتعدية

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham does not bother to refute Nimrod's sham claim to give life and death, signaling that its falsity is so obvious it needs no response.
rows.anchor: ولم يلتفت عليه السلام إلى إبطاله مقالة اللعين إيذانا بأن بطلانها من الجلاء والظهور
